/docs/help/create-first-openinterview: Create Your First OpenInterview (Right Side)Overview Upload Your Resume Resume Processing Generated Profile Overview Profile Header & Actions Video Section Profile Summary Card Bookings (Calendar) Attachments & Connect Highlights Resume Preview Next Steps (Edit, Video, Availability, Share)>ContentCreate Your First OpenInterviewCreate your first OpenInterview by uploading your resume, letting the platform generate your initial profile, and then refining the content before sharing it publicly.What this guide coversThis guide walks through the first part of the OpenInterview setup flow:Upload your resume Wait while your resume is processed Review the generated profile Understand each section of the new profile page Move to the next step: editing, video, calendar, and sharing Before you beginMake sure you have:an up-to-date resume in PDF format your preferred role title and summary in mind a headshot, profile image, or intro video ready if you plan to personalize the page further Step 1: Upload your resumeOn the OpenInterview creation page, start by uploading your resume using the upload box.What you will seeThe page includes:a large headline introducing the OpenInterview experience a drag-and-drop upload area a Browse Files button for manual upload How to uploadYou can upload your resume in either of two ways:Drag and dropDrag your resume file directly into the upload box.Browse filesClick Browse Files and select your resume from your device.What happens after uploadOnce the file is accepted:the file name appears below the upload area OpenInterview begins processing the document automatically you move into the resume analysis stage Step 2: Resume processingAfter upload, OpenInterview analyzes your resume and prepares your first profile draft.What the processing screen showsThe processing state includes:the uploaded file name a progress bar a percentage indicator a status message such as “Finalizing setup...” What OpenInterview is doing during this stepAt this stage, the platform is extracting and organizing information from your resume, including:your name current or target role location professional summary key highlights resume content profile-ready formatting for the public page What to expectProcessing usually results in:a structured profile layout automatically generated content blocks a profile page that is ready for review and editing Step 3: Review your generated profileOnce processing is complete, OpenInterview takes you to your newly created profile page.This page is your first live interview profile draft. It is already populated with information from your resume and structured into shareable sections.At this stage, the profile is meant to give you a strong starting point. You will still review and edit it before sharing.Profile page overviewThe generated profile page is organized into a main content area and a right-side profile panel.Top action barAt the top of the page, you will see a welcome banner and primary actions.What this section includesa greeting with your name a short message explaining this is your public interview page an Edit Profile button a Share button What this section meansThis is the control area for your profile.Edit ProfileUsed to refine and update each section of the page.ShareUsed later, after your profile is ready to publish and distribute.At this stage, the most important next action is Edit Profile.Main video sectionThe large video area is the centerpiece of the profile page.What this section is forThis is where your OpenInterview video introduction will appear.What you see initiallyBefore uploading a video, this section may display:a placeholder player state a thumbnail area a play button overlay What it becomes laterAfter you upload your video, this section becomes the main recorded introduction recruiters and employers will watch first.Why it mattersThis is the most important personal element on the page because it turns your resume into a more human, differentiated profile.Right-side profile cardThe right column contains your core candidate summary.What this section includesprofile image or avatar full name role title location short professional summary How it is generatedThis content is initially pulled from your resume and arranged into a concise candidate snapshot.What to review hereYou should check:name formatting title accuracy location accuracy summary tone and clarity Why this section mattersThis is the fastest way for a viewer to understand who you are and what type of role you fit.Bookings panelBelow the profile summary card is the bookings calendar section.What this section is forThis is where viewers will eventually see your interview availability and request time with you.What you may see initiallyAt this stage, the calendar may show:a month view timezone information no available slots yet Why it is empty at firstAvailability has not been configured yet. This will be set during the next step when you edit the profile and define your calendar schedule.What happens laterAfter availability is configured, this section becomes your live booking area.Attachments sectionOn the left side under the main video area, you may see an Attachments section.What this section is forThis area is used to display supporting files that help strengthen your profile.Examples of attachmentsportfolio files certifications work samples supplemental documents What you may see initiallyIf nothing has been uploaded yet, this section may show that no attachments are available.Connect sectionBelow Attachments is the Connect section.What this section is forThis area gives viewers additional ways to learn about you or connect with your professional presence.Common exampleLinkedIn profile link Why it mattersThis helps extend your profile beyond the OpenInterview page and gives recruiters another trusted source of professional context.Highlights sectionThe Highlights section presents your experience in quick, readable bullet points.What this section includesThis content is generated from your resume and may include:years of experience technical strengths role specialization workflow or domain expertise collaboration or leadership strengths Why this section mattersIt gives hiring teams a fast scan of your strongest qualifications without reading the full resume first.What to reviewYou should confirm:the bullets are accurate the most important strengths are represented the wording matches how you want to present yourself Resume sectionFurther down the page, the full resume is embedded directly into the profile.What this section includesa preview of the uploaded resume the original file name a Download Resume button What this is forThis lets viewers:read the full resume without leaving the page download it directly if needed Why it mattersIt combines the benefits of a modern profile page with the practicality of a traditional resume.What OpenInterview has done for you so farBy the time you reach this page, OpenInterview has already:accepted your uploaded resume processed the document extracted your core candidate details created a formatted public profile structure generated summary content and highlights embedded your resume into the page prepared a booking section for future availability setup This gives you a complete starting point rather than a blank profile.What to review before editingBefore clicking Edit Profile, review the generated page for:Identity detailscorrect name correct role title correct city or location Summary qualityaccurate positioning clear wording professional tone Highlightsstrongest points included phrasing aligned with your goals Resume previewcorrect file readable formatting correct download behavior Page completenesswhether you want attachments whether you want external links such as LinkedIn whether the profile is ready for a video and calendar setup Next step: Edit your profileOnce your initial profile has been created, the next step is to click Edit Profile.In the editing flow, you will:refine the wording in each section update your summary and highlights add or revise links and attachments set calendar availability upload your profile video prepare the page for sharing What comes nextThe next stage of setup is where your draft becomes a polished, public-facing OpenInterview profile.This includes:final verbiage video upload booking availability sharing your profile link

/docs/help/share-profile: Share Your OpenInterview Profile (Right Side)Overview Return to Profile Page Share Button Share Modal Overview Share via Email Add a Personal Message (Optional) Send Invite Copy Profile Link When to Share Best Practices Share Your OpenInterview ProfileOnce your profile is complete and saved, you can share it with recruiters, hiring managers, or anyone reviewing your candidacy.What this step isThis step allows you to distribute your OpenInterview profile using:direct email invitations a shareable profile link Your profile is now fully live and ready to be viewed.When to share your profileYou should share your profile after:completing all sections (bio, highlights, experience) uploading your video introduction setting your availability (if using bookings) Return to your profile pageAfter clicking Save Updates in the Edit Profile screen, you are returned to your public profile page.What you will seeYour profile now includes:your video (if uploaded) updated bio and highlights resume preview profile image booking calendar (if configured) At the top of the page, you will see two main actions:Edit Profile Share Share buttonClick the Share button to open the sharing interface.What this doesOpens a modal window Allows you to send or copy your profile Share modal overviewThe Share Profile modal includes two primary ways to share your profile:Send via email Copy a direct link Share via emailYou can send your profile directly to someone’s inbox.FieldsEmailEnter the recipient’s email address.Message (optional)Add a short message to personalize your outreach.Example message“Hi, I’d love for you to take a look at my OpenInterview profile. It includes a video introduction and highlights of my experience.”Send inviteClick Send Invite to email your profile.What happensThe recipient receives a link to your profile Your message (if included) is sent with it They can immediately view your profile Copy profile linkAlternatively, you can copy a direct link to your profile.How to useClick Copy Link to ProfileWhat you can do with the linkpaste into job applications send via LinkedIn messages include in email outreach add to your resume or portfolio When to use each optionUse email sharing when:you are applying directly to a recruiter you want a personalized introduction you are following up after a conversation Use link sharing when:applying through job portals networking on LinkedIn sharing broadly across channels What recruiters seeWhen someone opens your profile, they will see:your video introduction your professional summary key highlights resume preview and download attachments (if included) booking calendar (if enabled) Best practices for sharingKeep your message short and directAvoid long explanations. Let your profile do the work.Always include your videoProfiles with video significantly increase engagement.Tailor your message when possibleA personalized message improves response rates.Use your link consistentlyInclude it in:job applications email signatures LinkedIn outreach You’re now liveAt this point, your OpenInterview profile is:complete shareable ready for recruiters This replaces the traditional static resume with a dynamic, interactive profile.
